# A simultaneous projective minimum for centroidal central sections

This is a proved geometric invariant. No implication to the desired
weighted cap inequality is asserted.

Let K⊂R^d be a convex body with0 in its interior. For

    Ω={ℓ∈R^d:1+ℓ·x>0 for every x∈K}

and ℓ∈Ω define

    T_ℓ(x)=x/(1+ℓ·x),       K(ℓ)=T_ℓ(K).

Then K(ℓ) is a convex body containing0 in its interior. Every central
linear subspace and every central halfspace is preserved setwise by
T_ℓ. In particular the same oriented central planes can be used for
all K(ℓ).

## 1. Convexity and Jacobians

The map sends each segment to the segment with the same two image
endpoints, with positive reparametrized weights. Its inverse is T_{−ℓ}
on its image, so K(ℓ) is convex and compact. Direct differentiation,
or the rank-one determinant formula, gives

    det DT_ℓ(x)=(1+ℓ·x)^{−(d+1)}.

On an m-dimensional linear subspace E the restricted Jacobian is
(1+ℓ·x)^{−(m+1)}. Thus for Q=K∩E,

    |T_ℓ(Q)|_m = ∫_Q (1+ℓ·x)^{−(m+1)} dx.             (1)

For ℓ in a compact subset of Ω, differentiation under this integral is
justified by a uniform positive lower bound on all denominators. The
first and second derivatives in directions a,b are

    D_a|T_ℓ(Q)|_m
      =−(m+1)∫_Q (a·x)(1+ℓ·x)^{−(m+2)}dx,

    D_aD_b|T_ℓ(Q)|_m
      =(m+1)(m+2)∫_Q(a·x)(b·x)(1+ℓ·x)^{−(m+3)}dx.   (2)

The second derivative is positive semidefinite. If Q has nonempty
relative interior in E, its kernel consists exactly of directions
orthogonal to E. The domain Ω is convex.

## 2. Every centroidal section is simultaneously minimized at zero

Let u be a nonzero normal, Q=K∩u^⊥, and suppose the centroid of Q is0.
For d≥2, apply (2) with m=d−1. The gradient at ℓ=0 is zero, so convexity
implies the exact inequality

    |K(ℓ)∩u^⊥|_{d−1} ≥ |K∩u^⊥|_{d−1}
                         for every ℓ∈Ω.              (3)

Equality holds if and only if ℓ is parallel to u. Indeed the integrand
is strictly convex along any direction whose restriction to u^⊥ is
nonzero. Parallel ℓ leaves every x∈u^⊥ fixed. These assertions hold
simultaneously for every central section whose centroid is0.

For d=1, the central section is the singleton{0}, its H_0 measure is1,
and it is unchanged by every T_ℓ.

Consequently any positive weighted sum of these section areas is
minimized at ℓ=0. If the normals are not all parallel, the minimum is
strict, since the common equality directions consist only of0.

## 3. The full volume has an attained centroid-zero projective minimum

The function

    V(ℓ)=|K(ℓ)|=∫_K(1+ℓ·x)^{−(d+1)}dx

is strictly convex on Ω by (2), because K has nonempty interior.
It tends to infinity when ℓ tends to the boundary of Ω. Here is a
self-contained coercivity argument.

Choose r>0 with rB⊂K. Then Ω is bounded by1/r. Let ℓ_k tend to a
boundary point ℓ_*, and choose x_0∈K with1+ℓ_*·x_0=0. Put
δ_k=1+ℓ_k·x_0>0; then δ_k→0. Take a fixed small(d−1)-disk D centered
at0 in ℓ_*^⊥ and contained in rB. The cone conv(x_0,D) lies in K.
Its points x=(1−t)x_0+t z, z∈D,0≤t≤1, have volume element a positive
constant times t^{d−1}dt dz. Since ℓ_k are bounded,

    1+ℓ_k·x ≤ δ_k+C t

for a common finite C. Integrating over δ_k≤t≤2δ_k therefore gives
V(ℓ_k)≥c/δ_k for a fixed c>0 and all sufficiently large k. This diverges.
For d=1 the disk is a singleton and the same one-dimensional integral
has the same estimate.

A sublevel set is therefore compactly contained in Ω, and V attains a
unique minimum at some ℓ_*. At that minimum, (2) and the change of
variables z=T_{ℓ_*}(x) give

    0=∇V(ℓ_*)
     =−(d+1)∫_K x(1+ℓ_*·x)^{−(d+2)}dx
     =−(d+1)∫_{K(ℓ_*)} z dz.

Thus the ordinary centroid of K(ℓ_*) is0. Equivalently,
K(ℓ)^∘=K^∘+ℓ, since z·T_ℓ(x)≤1 is equivalent to(z−ℓ)·x≤1.
The preceding argument does not rely on a named polar-volume theorem.

## 4. What remains missing for the weighted cap inequality

For a fixed central halfspace H_i, its transformed volume is

    F_i(ℓ)=∫_{K∩H_i}(1+ℓ·x)^{−(d+1)}dx.

This is convex too, but its gradient depends on the first moment of
the entire cap, which need not vanish. Equation(3) controls the section
areas S_i(ℓ), not these cap volumes. If initially Σ_iθ_i S_i(0)u_i=0,
then reweighting by θ_i S_i(0)/S_i(ℓ) restores balance for K(ℓ), but it
also changes the weighted cap average. No inequality comparing that
new average with the original one has been proved here. The existence
of the centroid-zero projective image and simultaneous section-area
minima alone must not be presented as a proof of the desired constant.
